living_register_note: Per the Round 7 work order's §XIX: this register is a source-of-truth, not a one-time report. blockers.description: An RFC 3161 trusted timestamp relationship with a Time-Stamping Authority independent of VERIQO and of every party to a matter. VERIQO's self-hosted facility is a tamper-evident temporal chain: it proves ordering and non-alteration within the chain and proves nothing about wall-clock time.
blockers.code_requirement: pkg/platform/timestamp: the distinction is implemented and enforced. Kind.ProvesExistenceBefore() returns true only for IndependentAttestation; Attestation.Kind is derived by Assess and is not settable; a TSA operated by any party to the matter is refused and the downgrade is disclosed.
blockers.infrastructure_requirement: A commercial TSA account and network reachability to its RFC 3161 endpoint. Neither exists; this sandbox has no TSA relationship.
blockers.security_requirement: The TSA's signing certificate chain must validate to a trusted root, and the token must be stored verbatim so a third party can verify it without trusting VERIQO's parsing.
blockers.operational_requirement: Token acquisition at evidence finalization, retention of the tokens for the evidential lifetime, and a re-timestamping policy before the TSA's certificate expires.
blockers.external_evidence_required: A real RFC 3161 token, issued by a named authority independent of VERIQO and of the parties, covering a real evidence digest.
blockers.acceptance_criteria: A real token from a named independent TSA verifies against its certificate chain and raises a real evidence version's attestation to INDEPENDENT_ATTESTATION through timestamp.Assess, with no code change required to accept it.
blockers.owner: Repository owner: procure a TSA relationship (e.g. an accredited commercial timestamping service).
blockers.next_action: Procure a TSA account and wire its endpoint into evidence finalization. The typed landing place already exists; nothing in the code needs to change to accept a real token.

blockers.description: An independent assessor's examination of VERIQO's evidence-handling controls and qualification procedure. This is the third level of proof: PROOF_OBJECT_CREATED != PROOF_QUALIFIED != PROOF_EXTERNALLY_ATTESTED. VERIQO can reach the second level alone and can never reach the third.
blockers.code_requirement: pkg/proof: the three levels are implemented. RaiseToExternallyAttested requires a sealed, qualified object, an attestation pinning its hash, and a named attestor who is not VERIQO or any party to the matter. No VERIQO code path calls it.
blockers.infrastructure_requirement: None. This blocker is not technical: it needs an assessor, not a deployment.
blockers.security_requirement: The attestor's identity and reference must be recorded, and the attestation must pin the exact proof object hash examined.
blockers.operational_requirement: An engagement with an assessor competent in evidence handling, and a re-assessment cycle when the qualification procedure changes.
blockers.external_evidence_required: A signed statement from a named, competent assessor that VERIQO's qualification procedure was correctly applied to a specific proof object.
blockers.acceptance_criteria: A named assessor's signed statement raises a real proof object to PROOF_EXTERNALLY_ATTESTED through proof.RaiseToExternallyAttested, and the constitutional proof audit records its first QUALIFIED article.
blockers.owner: Repository owner: engage an independent assessor with evidence-handling competence.
blockers.artifact: pkg/proof/attestation.go, pkg/assurance (the constitutional proof audit: 0 of 30 articles QUALIFIED)
blockers.next_action: Engage an assessor. Until one has examined a control, no article in the constitutional proof audit can reach QUALIFIED, and no proof object can be described as proved.
